rv.q: What he lacks in dramatic presence, Antonenko compensates for in vocal intensity.

Nézet-Séguin and Sher have obviously worked closely to realize Verdi's vision of musical drama: A vampiric Otello approaches Desdemona's bed and grabs a pillow to the menacing sound of a string tremolo.
Sonya Yoncheva gave the opera's most devastating and gorgeous performance.
The performances of Yoncheva, Lučić, and Nezet-Séguin alone are grounds to call this opening night a triumph, and they should be able to carry this new production through the end of its run.
This Otello is a successful, if restrained take on an opera that is typically filled with more passion than a single stage can hold.
I would argue that if this isn’t an ideal Otello , it’s a production that brings a much chest-voiced excitement to the Met stage.

cn.t: Critics praise this new Met production of Verdi's masterpiece, commending the talented musical performances and Yannick Nézet-Séguin's conducting that elevate the occasionally restrained but imaginative staging.
